nina: Hi team, new here — trying to bring up the dev stack with docker compose. web can't connect to Postgres (Connection refused). `docker compose ps` shows postgres container exits and restarts. I'm on Ubuntu with a system Postgres running. Any tips?

Carlos: Welcome! :wave: Quick check: did you map the host port 5432 in compose? If the host Postgres is already bound to 5432 the container will fail to bind that port. Post the compose snippet.

nina: Yep here's the postgres service from compose.yml

nina: ```yaml
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:14
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    environment:
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: example
      POSTGRES_DB: myapp_dev
    volumes:
      - ./pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
```

Irene (infra): That explains it. If your host already has a postgres process listening on 5432, Docker can't bind the same host port. The container will crash with bind errors and you'll see repeated restarts. Check `sudo ss -ltnp | grep 5432` or `ss -ltnp | grep postgres` to confirm.

Carlos: Two options: 1) Stop the host postgres (e.g., `sudo systemctl stop postgresql`) while you run the compose stack, or 2) change the host mapping to a different port like `5433:5432` so the container's internal 5432 is exposed as 5433 on the host. For services inside compose you actually don't need the `ports:` mapping at all — remove it and other containers will still reach `db:5432` via the compose network.

nina: I removed the ports mapping (didn't realize internal services didn't need it) and the db container now stays up. But when I exec into web and run `psql -h db -U postgres -d myapp_dev` I get `psql: could not connect to server: No such file or directory`.

Irene (infra): If you removed ports and exec into the web container, use the service hostname `db` (you did) and ensure the env var in web points to the same DB name and user. Also check the postgres logs; if the volume `./pgdata` was created by root earlier you can get permission issues and postgres may initdb on first run then exit. `docker logs <db_container>` will show if initdb failed or if permissions were changed.

nina: Logs showed `could not open PID file: Permission denied` and some `initdb` warnings. I had run docker-compose earlier with `sudo` and now the ./pgdata folder is owned by root.

Carlos: Yep that's the classic one. Fix with `sudo chown -R $(id -u):$(id -g) ./pgdata` from your host shell (or recreate the volume). Then `docker compose down -v` and `docker compose up` again so postgres can initialize correctly.

nina: Did that and restarted without `sudo`. DB is up and app connects. Thanks! :tada: Also changed local mapping to `5433:5432` in a dev override so my host postgres can stay running when I need it.

devbot: Tip: update onboarding README with common local pitfalls: host port conflicts, avoid running compose with sudo (permission issues on bind mounts), and prefer removing `ports:` for internal-only services. :memo:
